{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible as a controlled soil-texture sensitivity experiment; drainage response is a model diagnostic, not validated against observations.",
    "answerable": [
      "Relative sensitivity of ELM-simulated sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture under identical climate forcing",
      "Ranking of texture classes by seasonal and annual drainage partitioning versus surface runoff",
      "Water-table and soil-moisture response across a sand-to-clay gradient"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Absolute validation of tile-drain flow magnitudes (no tile-drain observations available)",
      "Explicit tile-drainage management effects (ELM lacks calibrated tile-drain parameterization here)",
      "Spatially distributed basin-wide drainage mapping (single-column archetype, not fully gridded)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "Six columns isolate the soil-texture control by holding climate, topography, and vegetation fixed while stepping through a coarse-to-fine texture gradient (sand, sandy loam, loam, silt loam, silty clay loam, clay). This spans the dominant agricultural soils of the Upper Iowa loess/till landscape and yields a clean monotonic sensitivity signal for QDRAI.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "UI_sand",          "lat": 43.45, "lon": -92.30, "soil_texture": "sand"},
    {"id": "UI_sandy_loam",    "lat": 43.42, "lon": -92.10, "soil_texture": "sandy loam"},
    {"id": "UI_loam",          "lat": 43.40, "lon": -91.90, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "UI_silt_loam",     "lat": 43.38, "lon": -91.70, "soil_texture": "silt loam"},
    {"id": "UI_silty_clay_loam","lat": 43.36, "lon": -91.55, "soil_texture": "silty clay loam"},
    {"id": "UI_clay",          "lat": 43.34, "lon": -91.40, "soil_texture": "clay"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI",
      "QDRAI_PERCH",
      "QOVER",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QINFL",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "ZWT",
      "ZWT_PERCH",
      "H2OSOI",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "WA",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QFLX_EVAP_TOT",
      "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "single-column ELM (I-compartment, satellite phenology or BGC)",
    "GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing 1980-2018 for the Upper Iowa bbox",
    "user-specified soil-texture override (sand/clay percent by layer)",
    "surface dataset generation (mksurfdata) with prescribed crop/managed-vegetation PFT"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "STOP_N interpreted in years (STOP_OPTION=nyears) preceded by an accelerated-decomposition/hydrologic spin-up cycling 1980-1999 forcing",
    "All columns forced with the same climate to isolate texture as the sole varying driver",
    "Agricultural land cover represented via a rainfed managed-crop PFT with uniform topography and slope",
    "Texture classes mapped to representative sand/silt/clay fractions applied uniformly through the soil column",
    "No explicit engineered tile-drain module; QDRAI serves as the sub-surface drainage proxy",
    "Elevation/slope held constant so drainage differences reflect hydraulic properties, not topography"
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as a controlled soil-texture sensitivity experiment; drainage response is a model diagnostic, not validated against observations.
answerable: Relative sensitivity of ELM-simulated sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture under identical climate forcing
Ranking of texture classes by seasonal and annual drainage partitioning versus surface runoff
Water-table and soil-moisture response across a sand-to-clay gradient
not_answerable: Absolute validation of tile-drain flow magnitudes (no tile-drain observations available)
Explicit tile-drainage management effects (ELM lacks calibrated tile-drain parameterization here)
Spatially distributed basin-wide drainage mapping (single-column archetype, not fully gridded)

parsed.n_justification: Six columns isolate the soil-texture control by holding climate, topography, and vegetation fixed while stepping through a coarse-to-fine texture gradient (sand, sandy loam, loam, silt loam, silty clay loam, clay). This spans the dominant agricultural soils of the Upper Iowa loess/till landscape and yields a clean monotonic sensitivity signal for QDRAI.
requires_capabilities: single-column ELM (I-compartment, satellite phenology or BGC)
GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing 1980-2018 for the Upper Iowa bbox
user-specified soil-texture override (sand/clay percent by layer)
surface dataset generation (mksurfdata) with prescribed crop/managed-vegetation PFT
assumptions: STOP_N interpreted in years (STOP_OPTION=nyears) preceded by an accelerated-decomposition/hydrologic spin-up cycling 1980-1999 forcing
All columns forced with the same climate to isolate texture as the sole varying driver
Agricultural land cover represented via a rainfed managed-crop PFT with uniform topography and slope
Texture classes mapped to representative sand/silt/clay fractions applied uniformly through the soil column
No explicit engineered tile-drain module; QDRAI serves as the sub-surface drainage proxy
Elevation/slope held constant so drainage differences reflect hydraulic properties, not topography
